purpose: the simplest law that keeps IOTA's defining ingredients (an exact integer amplitude ledger, unspent vacuum budget, activation by transfer, exhaustion into a depleted medium) and nothing else; the registered persistence test runs on this law, and every richer IOTA mechanism is added back later one rung at a time
kept_from_iota: integer amplitude quanta with an exact conserved ledger (v0.2 law L1)
latent vacuum budget absorbed on activation (v0.2 law L2)
exhaustion deactivation leaving a permanently depleted site (v0.2 law L3)

deliberately_deferred.reason: with a strict a_y < a_x rule, a one-quantum transfer between amplitudes 3 and 2 reverses the gradient and can oscillate forever, so absorption is no longer guaranteed in a finite region; even a non-reversing a_y <= a_x - 2 rule admits no simple monotone potential under simultaneous many-to-one transfers. It returns as ladder rung 1 with its own termination audit.

removed_from_iota: vector states, vector behaviour bands, and vector-directed primary targets
range R and inverse-square influence decay
amplitude_coupling gates (every eligible transfer fires; see 'control parameter')
angular memory, received rotation, and residual angular bias
the sequential lexicographic scheduler (replaced by a synchronous tick)

state_per_site.a: integer active amplitude >= 0; the site is active iff a >= 1
state_per_site.l: integer latent budget in {0, v}; always 0 at an active site

control_parameter.name: rho
control_parameter.meaning: vacuum occupation: the probability that a non-seed site starts fresh rather than depleted
control_parameter.why_this_parameter: rho is a genuine probability of the medium, not a rate, so it cannot be absorbed into a rescaling of time (the defect found in the amplitude_coupling path); it is the site-occupation parameter of the fresh medium

initial_state.medium: every other site independently fresh with probability rho, otherwise depleted; drawn from the run's medium RNG stream before tick 1

L0.ledger: sum over sites of (a + l) is exactly constant at every tick
tick: 1. Read the tick-start state S_t; nothing below reads a partially updated state.
2. For each active site x, in lexicographic (x, y, z) order, form its eligible set E_x = { y in face6(x) : y is fresh }.

3. If E_x is non-empty, order E_x by the fixed neighbour order (+x, -x, +y, -y, +z, -z), draw one u = rng.random() from the run's dynamics stream, and record one quantum x -> E_x[floor(u * |E_x|)]. Draws are consumed in lexicographic source order, one per source with non-empty E_x, so any two correct implementations agree bit for bit. Each active site sends at most one quantum per tick. Sites with empty E_x draw nothing.
4. Apply all recorded quanta simultaneously: each source's a decreases by 1. Only fresh sites receive quanta in L0.
5. A fresh site that received k >= 1 quanta (from k distinct sources) becomes active with a = v + k and l = 0 (activation absorbs its own budget; no amplitude is created).
6. Exhaustion: any site with a = 0 after step 4 that was active at tick start becomes depleted (l = 0).

absorbing_certificate.definition: no active site has a fresh face neighbour
absorbing_certificate.exactness: if the certificate holds, step 3 records no quanta, so S_(t+1) = S_t and the certificate holds again; the state is absorbing. If it fails, at least one quantum moves with probability 1. The certificate is therefore exact and needs no simulation.

L0.active_unit: a site that sends or receives a quantum during the tick
facts_by_construction: total active amplitude never decreases: each activation adds v = 2
activity ends exactly when no active site borders a fresh site; amplitude left in active sites with no fresh neighbour is stranded

transfers go only into fresh sites, every tick with a transfer activates at least one fresh site, and each fresh site activates once; so the number of ticks with any transfer is at most the number of fresh sites in the seed's adjacent fresh clusters, and a run on a finite cluster always terminates
the set of sites ever activated lies inside the union of face6 fresh-site clusters adjacent to the seed
for rho below the simple-cubic site-percolation threshold those clusters are finite almost surely, so every run is absorbed

exploration can be incomplete above threshold: an activated site holds a = v + k, typically 3, and can serve at most that many of its up to 5 fresh neighbours before exhausting; unserved neighbours are reached only by other routes. Whether this budget limit shifts the persistence threshold above the percolation threshold is the primary registered question

L1.definition: L0 plus reactivation: in step 2, each depleted face neighbour y of x is also placed in E_x independently with probability r per (x, y) pair per tick; a depleted site receiving k quanta becomes active with a = k

analytic_result.statement: for every r > 0 and every rho, IOTA-MIN-L1 has no absorbing state reachable before wrap contact, so single-seed activity never dies
analytic_result.argument: total active amplitude is at least a0 >= 1 forever, so an active set exists; any finite active set has a boundary site with an inactive face neighbour; that neighbour is fresh (eligible with probability 1) or depleted (eligible with probability r > 0); so every tick has positive probability of a transfer and the certificate never holds
analytic_result.consequence_for_iota: with an exact amplitude ledger, any reactivation channel makes lattice activity immortal. Persistence questions about IOTA's canonical laws (residual recruitment > 0) therefore cannot be about whether activity survives; they must be about whether a specific organization or role survives (deferred stage R)
analytic_result.verification_required: the freeze must include a written proof check and a synthetic-state test of the boundary argument

L1.draw_rule: for each active source in lexicographic order and each depleted neighbour in the fixed neighbour order, draw one u = rng.random() and include the neighbour iff u < r; then draw the target as in L0 step 3 from the same stream
